title: ACA 13 (Ward) — Protect and Retain the Majority Vote Act
summary_title: Protect and Retain the Majority Vote Act
summary_text: Would require that ballot measures proposing to increase voting thresholds for future measures must themselves pass by the same increased threshold they seek to impose. Currently, a simple majority can pass a measure requiring supermajority votes for future actions, giving disproportionate power to a minority of voters. The measure aims to prevent abuse of the initiative process and protect local control by ensuring that statewide voters cannot easily override local decision-making with artificially high voting requirements.
briefing_text: ACA 13, the Protect and Retain the Majority Vote Act, would require that any ballot measure seeking to increase voting thresholds for future measures must pass by the same threshold it seeks to impose. Currently, a simple majority can pass measures requiring supermajority votes for future actions, which the measure's supporters argue gives disproportionate power to minority voters. The constitutional amendment aims to prevent abuse of the initiative process and protect local control from statewide override. It requires a simple majority (50%) to pass and was placed on the ballot by the state legislature.

measure_id: SCA 1 (Newman) Elections: recall of state officers
title: SCA 1 (Newman) — Recall Process Reform
summary_text: Would reform California's recall process by eliminating the simultaneous successor election that currently appears on recall ballots. Under the current system, voters decide both whether to recall an officer and who should replace them, allowing a replacement to be chosen by a slim plurality rather than majority support. If adopted, when a state officer is recalled, the office would be filled according to existing constitutional succession rules (such as the Lieutenant Governor becoming Governor), removing what supporters call political gamesmanship from the recall process.
briefing_text: SCA 1 would fundamentally change California's recall process by eliminating the current two-question ballot where voters decide both whether to recall an official and select a replacement. Under this reform, recalled officials would be replaced through existing constitutional succession procedures rather than a simultaneous election. Supporters argue this prevents candidates from winning with small pluralities and reduces political manipulation of the recall process. The measure requires a simple majority (50%) to pass.
pro_arguments: ["Prevents replacement candidates from winning with a small plurality rather than majority support (CalBallot)", "Removes political gamesmanship from the recall process by using established succession rules (CalBallot)"]

summary_text: This ballot measure would establish a public campaign financing system in California, allowing eligible candidates to receive government funding for their campaigns instead of relying solely on private donations. The measure implements the California Fair Elections Act of 2026 as an amendment to the existing Political Reform Act of 1974.
briefing_text: SB 42, the California Fair Elections Act of 2026, would create a public campaign financing system allowing eligible candidates to receive government funding rather than relying solely on private donations. Authored by Senator Tom Umberg, this legislative statute would amend the Political Reform Act of 1974. The measure requires a simple majority (50%) to pass. California voters have considered 20 similar campaign finance measures in the past, with mixed results depending on the specific provisions and political context.

The legislature would then have an opportunity to consider and potentially enact the measure before signature collection continues. The measure requires a simple majority to pass. summary_text: This measure would make permanent the existing temporary tax rates on high-income earners that are currently set to expire in 2031, applying to income over approximately $360,000-$721,000 depending on filing status. The measure would maintain $5-15 billion in annual state income tax revenue, with 89% allocated to K-12 schools and 11% to community colleges.
briefing_text: This ballot measure would make permanent the temporary tax rates on high-income Californians earning over approximately $360,000-$721,000 (depending on filing status) that are currently set to expire in 2031. The measure would maintain $5-15 billion annually in state revenue, with 89% allocated to K-12 schools and 11% to community colleges. Local school boards would control spending decisions, though administrative costs are prohibited. The measure requires a simple majority to pass and would also increase General Fund revenues available for education, healthcare, budget reserves, and other programs.
fiscal_impact: The measure would maintain $5 billion to $15 billion of annual state income taxes (in today's dollars) by making a tax on high income earners permanent instead of letting it expire in 2031 (Legislative Analyst and Director of Finance).
